about: Speaker decisions a person made where the projection or Glyssen could not (SOP 2C). Each verse's lines must rejoin to the verse exactly; tests check it. Settled 2026-10-07 from Glyssen's own candidates, the surrounding text, and the speakers of the neighbouring verses.

lines: And one went in, and told his lord, saying,
Thus and thus said the maid that is of the land of Israel.
2KI 5:4.reason: Glyssen's first candidate: Naaman reports the girl's words to his king (5:5 answers him).

lines: Bless ye God in the congregations, even the Lord, from the fountain of Israel.
PSA 68:26.reason: The Psalms are read by the narrator; Glyssen's other candidates are only hypothetical.

lines: Draw me, we will run after thee: the king hath brought me into his chambers: we will be glad and rejoice in thee, we will remember thy love more than wine: the upright love thee.
SNG 1:4.reason: Glyssen leaves the Song's speakers open; our script reads the Song with the narrator except where Glyssen names a speaker, so these verses match their neighbours (see decisions: the Song).

lines: If thou know not, O thou fairest among women, go thy way forth by the footsteps of the flock, and feed thy kids beside the shepherds’ tents.
We will make thee borders of gold with studs of silver.
The beams of our house are cedar, and our rafters of fir.
Take us the foxes, the little foxes, that spoil the vines: for our vines have tender grapes.
I am come into my garden, my sister, my spouse: I have gathered my myrrh with my spice; I have eaten my honeycomb with my honey; I have drunk my wine with my milk:
eat, O friends; drink, yea, drink abundantly, O beloved.
SNG 5:1.reason: Glyssen's reference script names both speakers here; the projection found no capital where the friends begin (poetry, no verb of speaking).

lines: Who is she that looketh forth as the morning, fair as the moon, clear as the sun, and terrible as an army with banners?
I went down into the garden of nuts to see the fruits of the valley, and to see whether the vine flourished, and the pomegranates budded.
Or ever I was aware, my soul made me like the chariots of Amminadib.
And the roof of thy mouth like the best wine for my beloved, that goeth down sweetly, causing the lips of those that are asleep to speak.
We have a little sister, and she hath no breasts: what shall we do for our sister in the day when she shall be spoken for?
If she be a wall, we will build upon her a palace of silver: and if she be a door, we will inclose her with boards of cedar.
All flesh is grass, and all the goodliness thereof is as the flower of the field:
ISA 40:6.reason: Glyssen's candidates: the commissioning voice (God, its alternate), the prophet's reply (Isaiah), and the voice's answer, which runs on through 40:8.

lines: The grass withereth, the flower fadeth: because the spirit of the LORD bloweth upon it: surely the people is grass.
The grass withereth, the flower fadeth: but the word of our God shall stand for ever.
So the carpenter encouraged the goldsmith, and he that smootheth with the hammer him that smote the anvil, saying,
It is ready for the sodering:
and he fastened it with nails, that it should not be moved.
ISA 41:7.reason: As the reference script, which the projection could not place; matches 41:5-6, where the narrator tells and the islanders speak.

lines: Who hath declared from the beginning, that we may know? and beforetime, that we may say, He is righteous? yea, there is none that sheweth, yea, there is none that declareth, yea, there is none that heareth your words.
ISA 41:26.reason: Within God's challenge to the idols (41:21 'saith the LORD' through 41:29); Glyssen's alternate.

lines: Return, ye backsliding children, and I will heal your backslidings.
Behold, we come unto thee; for thou art the LORD our God.
JER 3:22.reason: Glyssen names Israel (Normal) for the people's answer, which runs on through 3:25.

lines: Truly in vain is salvation hoped for from the hills, and from the multitude of mountains: truly in the LORD our God is the salvation of Israel.
For shame hath devoured the labour of our fathers from our youth; their flocks and their herds, their sons and their daughters.

We lie down in our shame, and our confusion covereth us: for we have sinned against the LORD our God, we and our fathers, from our youth even unto this day, and have not obeyed the voice of the LORD our God.
O LORD, though our iniquities testify against us, do thou it for thy name’s sake: for our backslidings are many; we have sinned against thee.
JER 14:7.reason: Jeremiah's prayer for the people: the LORD answers him in 14:11, 'Pray not for this people'.

lines: O the hope of Israel, the saviour thereof in time of trouble, why shouldest thou be as a stranger in the land, and as a wayfaring man that turneth aside to tarry for a night?
Why shouldest thou be as a man astonied, as a mighty man that cannot save? yet thou, O LORD, art in the midst of us, and we are called by thy name; leave us not.

For I heard the defaming of many, fear on every side. Report, say they, and we will report it. All my familiars watched for my halting, saying, Peradventure he will be enticed, and we shall prevail against him, and we shall take our revenge on him.
JER 20:10.reason: Jeremiah's lament (20:7-18) is read by the narrator in our script; the quoted enemies stay with whoever quotes them (SOP 2A.3).

lines: Jesus answered and said unto him,
Before that Philip called thee, when thou wast under the fig tree, I saw thee.
JHN 1:48.reason: Glyssen: Nathanael (puzzled) and Jesus; the projection failed on the first boundary and the red letter fixed only Christ's line.

lines: And they said unto them even as Jesus had commanded: and they let them go.
MRK 11:6.reason: Indirect speech in the KJV (Glyssen marks it Indirect).

lines: David therefore himself calleth him Lord; and whence is he then his son?
And the common people heard him gladly.
MRK 12:37.reason: eBible's red letter wraps the whole verse, but its last sentence is narration (a source error; the app's red letter has the same mistake).

lines: And when he knew it of the centurion, he gave the body to Joseph.
MRK 15:45.reason: Indirect speech in the KJV (Glyssen marks it Indirect).

lines: And the angel of the LORD said unto Balaam,
Go with the men: but only the word that I shall speak unto thee, that thou shalt speak.
So Balaam went with the princes of Balak.
NUM 22:35.reason: The angel's words run to 'that thou shalt speak.'; the projection cut them a clause early.

lines: And he arose early in the morning on the fifth day to depart: and the damsel’s father said,
Comfort thine heart, I pray thee.
And they tarried until afternoon, and they did eat both of them.
JDG 19:8.reason: 'I pray thee' belongs to the father's words; the projection cut them early.

lines: And Jonathan cried after the lad,
And Jonathan’s lad gathered up the arrows, and came to his master.
1SA 20:38.reason: 'Make speed, haste, stay not.' is all Jonathan's cry.

lines: And the messengers came again, and said,
messengers of Ben-Hadad, king of Aram
Thus speaketh Ben-hadad, saying, Although I have sent unto thee, saying, Thou shalt deliver me thy silver, and thy gold, and thy wives, and thy children;
1KI 20:5.reason: The messengers speak from 'Thus speaketh Ben-hadad'; the projection began their words a clause late.

lines: If thou return at all in peace, the LORD hath not spoken by me.
Hearken, O people, every one of you.
1KI 22:28.reason: 'And he said,' is the narrator's; Micaiah's second line is 'Hearken, O people, every one of you.'

lines: If thou certainly return in peace, then hath not the LORD spoken by me.
It is naught, it is naught,
saith the buyer: but when he is gone his way, then he boasteth.
PRO 20:14.reason: The buyer's words are 'It is naught, it is naught'; 'saith the buyer' is narration.

lines: And the vision of all is become unto you as the words of a book that is sealed, which men deliver to one that is learned, saying,
person asking someone to read a sealed book
I cannot; for it is sealed:
ISA 29:11.reason: 'I pray thee' belongs to the request.

lines: And the book is delivered to him that is not learned, saying,
person asking someone to read a sealed book
Wherefore have I seen them dismayed and turned away back? and their mighty ones are beaten down, and are fled apace, and look not back: for fear was round about,
JER 46:5.reason: Only 'saith the LORD.' is narration; 'for fear was round about' is the LORD's.

lines: Depart ye; it is unclean; depart, depart, touch not:
when they fled away and wandered, they said among the heathen,
They shall no more sojourn there.
LAM 4:15.reason: 'They cried unto them,' introduces the cry (the merge kept the introduction with the speakers).

lines: But Nineveh is of old like a pool of water: yet they shall flee away.
shall they cry; but none shall look back.
NAM 2:8.reason: The cry is 'Stand, stand'; 'shall they cry' is narration.

lines: And forthwith he came to Jesus, and said,
And as soon as he was come, he goeth straightway to him, and saith,
When ye pray, say, Our Father which art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name. Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done, as in heaven, so in earth.
LUK 11:2.reason: Christ's words begin at 'When ye pray, say,'; eBible's red letter starts at 'Our Father' (a source omission).

lines: I am Alpha and Omega, the beginning and the ending,
which is, and which was, and which is to come, the Almighty.
REV 1:8.reason: After 'saith the Lord,' the Lord's words resume; eBible's red letter marks only the first clause.

lines: voice of great crowd, like roar of many waters, loud thunderclaps
And to her was granted that she should be arrayed in fine linen, clean and white:
for the fine linen is the righteousness of saints.
REV 19:8.reason: 'clean and white:' completes the voice's words; the explanation that follows is narration (Glyssen's reference script).

lines: Come, and let us cut them off from being a nation; that the name of Israel may be no more in remembrance.
PSA 83:4.reason: The enemies' words begin at 'Come,' and run to the end; the projection cut them after 'Come,'.

JHN 1:21.reason: 'Art thou that prophet?' is the questioners' (no introduction in the KJV); the projection left it with the narrator.
